data.gender_notes: Shivpoojan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Shivpoojan is derived from the words Shiva (God of Destruction and Renewal) and Poojan (worship). This name signifies the act of dedicating oneself to the worship of Lord Shiva. It is a name that embodies devotion, spirituality, and a deep connection to the divine. The name Shivpoojan carries the meaning “Worship of Shiva” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi. Parents who choose Shivpoojan usually hope their child will grow to embody worship of shiva and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: This name represents the deep reverence and devotion towards Lord Shiva. It is a name that signifies the journey towards self-realization and spiritual growth.
data.etymology: Shivpoojan belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Worship of Shiva.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shivpoojan total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Shiva Pooja was an important ritual during the Shivaite period in ancient India, particularly during the Chalukya and Pallava dynasties (500-1200 CE). This period is marked by the flourishing of temple architecture, with major temples such as the Kailasa Temple at Ellora and the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram being built during this time.

Shiva Pooja also held significance during the medieval Bhakti movement (1100-1350 CE) when the devotional focus shifted from formal rituals to personal devotion towards the deity. This period saw the emergence of poet-saints like Tirumular, Appar, and Sambandar, who composed hymns in honor of Shiva.
